findings.finding: The new `/api/org/file?path=` proxy takes a browser-supplied path and adds a write verb (`PUT`) on the plain, unauthenticated `/api/` surface. It mirrors the shape of a secret-gated external route but drops the host+secret gate, so any process that can reach the server — or potentially a cross-site request if the app has cookies/CORS quirks — could read or modify files under `leadsRoot`.
findings.suggestion: Do not implement this as a general file proxy. Allowlist exactly the org docs this page needs (`charter.md`, `learnings.md`, `audit.jsonl`, `org-chart.json`, `conventions.md`, `principal.md`, `decision_log.md`), reject absolute paths and traversal, enforce containment under `config.leadsRoot`, and add same-origin/CSRF protection for the `PUT`. Confirm the server is bound to loopback if the broader web surface is intentionally unauthenticated.

findings.finding: /api/org/leads/:leadId/role` reads `charter.path` from the parsed `org-chart.json`. That path is file content, not a trusted route parameter. If the chart is malformed or malicious, the new route could be used to read arbitrary files outside `leadsRoot`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the exact existing org file-read containment helper; never implement a new raw `fs.readFile` path in `routes/org.ts`. Resolve the path, verify it starts with `leadsRoot` and is a regular file, and return a controlled 400/not-measured response on validation failure rather than forwarding the underlying error.

findings.finding: Widening `MarkdownEditorModal` from hardcoded `projectId`+`path` to an injected `{ load, save }` pair can break existing callers and existing modal tests unless the old calling mode remains supported or every caller is migrated in the same change.
findings.suggestion: Make the injected API optional and preserve the existing `projectId`/`path` path as the default, or explicitly list and update every existing caller. Also verify the new `orgMarkdownFileApi` maps the ETag/If-Match/412 conflict behavior exactly to the existing `MarkdownConflictError` contract.

findings.finding: The single `useOrgChartPresence()` hook must encode the acceptance criteria precisely: only true 404 hides the Org nav entry, while 502/500/network errors still show the entry. A naïve “if request failed, hide” implementation would fail the invalid-file acceptance case.
findings.suggestion: Define explicit hook states (`unknown`, `present`, `absent`) and use HTTP status classification, not generic success/error booleans. Sidebar/palette should render only after `present` is known, and direct `/org` navigation on a non-404 error should show the page-level error rather than redirecting away.

findings.finding: A lead card makes multiple sub-requests (`role`, `status`, `usage`). If any one of those endpoints fails, the current plan risks either failing the entire card or losing block ordering. The acceptance criteria require each block to be independently measured/unmeasured, including under partial failure.
findings.suggestion: Implement block-level error catching so a failed role/status/usage request renders that block as “not measured” or an explicit unavailable state, while the rest of the card remains intact and in the fixed five-block order. Component tests should cover one endpoint failing per block.

findings.finding: Shared documents are presented as fixed entries (`org-chart.json`, `conventions.md`, `principal.md`, `decision_log.md`), but the plan does not define what happens when one of those files is absent. The page should still render the shared-documents block rather than showing a blank/broken section.
findings.suggestion: Define missing-document behavior for the view links/rows, such as a visible “not found” state or disabled entry, and add it to the component tests.

findings.finding: “One sentence extracted from `charter.md`” is simple to state but easy to get subtly wrong with Markdown front matter, headings, bullets, links, or code fences. A naive split may return an empty, malformed, or misleading segment.
findings.suggestion: Specify the extraction rules explicitly: skip YAML front matter and heading lines, select the first plain non-heading prose paragraph, strip Markdown link/image syntax from the result, and return `{ measured: false }` if no usable prose sentence exists.  Overall assessment: The in-process server-side proxy approach is the right shape for this change, and the plan correctly avoids widening the external org contract. The main issues are around the unauthenticated file-write surface and path handling, plus several edge/error-isolation cases that should be tightened before build. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The new plain `/api/org/` route family exposes organization metadata and file contents that are currently behind the `x-shipwright-leads-secret` external-process boundary. In particular, charter content, learnings, and `audit.jsonl` may contain operationally sensitive material. Reusing an “unauthenticated `/api/` surface” is only safe if that surface is already protected by deployment/network controls appropriate for this data; the plan does not establish that.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly confirm and document the effective browser access boundary for the web UI in deployed environments. If `/api/` is reachable by untrusted users or networks, require the application’s existing authenticated-session/authorization mechanism for `/api/org/`, or constrain the route family to the same trusted origin/network deployment model. Do not rely on the absence of a new auth mechanism as proof that these files are safe to expose.

findings.finding: GET`/`PUT /api/org/file?path=` creates a practical arbitrary-file-read/write risk unless it has stricter authorization than merely resolving a path below `leadsRoot`. A caller could request another lead’s files, non-document files under the root, path-traversal variants, or symlinked files. The write endpoint is especially sensitive.
findings.suggestion: Do not treat this as a generic path proxy. Validate the requested path against the currently parsed org chart and a small explicit policy: shared documents are read-only and allowlisted; a lead may expose only its declared `charter.md`, `learnings.md`, and `audit.jsonl`; only the declared charter path is writable. Resolve canonical real paths, reject traversal and symlink escapes, and preserve the existing ETag/`If-Match` behavior. Add route tests for traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, unknown lead paths, read-only document writes, and a charter belonging to another lead.

findings.finding: The in-process route approach is sound, but it needs a clearly defined translation layer for errors and partial data. The proposed status endpoint combines `last-run` and `beat-register`; a read failure in one source must not accidentally turn a measurable state into “Resting,” a generic broken page, or a fabricated value. Likewise, a role-file read failure should be distinguishable from “no sentence found.”
findings.suggestion: Define response/error semantics before implementation. Return explicit per-field or per-source measured/error state where the UI can honestly render “not measured” versus a failure message. Preserve typed distinctions for unknown lead, missing source file, malformed register/usage data, and unexpected I/O failure. Ensure the page can retain chart/card rendering when an individual lead subresource fails.

findings.finding: The nav-gating behavior is specified, but the asynchronous behavior is not. A presence hook initially has no result; if the sidebar/palette hides Org during loading, the item may visibly flicker. More importantly, `/org` must not redirect merely because the presence request is still loading or temporarily retrying.
findings.suggestion: Model presence as at least `loading | present | missing | broken`. Redirect/hide `/org` only after a confirmed `org_chart_missing` 404. Keep Org visible for loading, invalid-chart, and other failure states; render a deliberate page-level loading or error state. Disable or carefully configure retries so a confirmed 404 is not repeatedly requested, while transient failures remain recoverable. Test the route guard separately from the nav components.

findings.finding: The plan states that docs are wired, but only specifies reuse of `MarkdownEditorModal` for charter editing. It does not identify the existing component/API behavior for view-only `learnings.md` and especially `audit.jsonl`, which is not Markdown. Rendering either as unbounded raw text would be a poor operational UX and could create performance issues for a growing audit log.
findings.suggestion: Identify and reuse an existing read-only document/modal viewer if one exists. Otherwise define the minimum display contract: safe text rendering, bounded initial content or pagination for audit logs, loading/error states, and no edit affordance. Ensure the org file route supplies the correct content type/format or an explicit document-kind field rather than making the client infer it solely from a path.

findings.finding: The Stats data contract is underspecified. The card promises five figures—cadence, parallelism, 7-day budget, projects, and runs—but the proposed sources explicitly account for cadence from last-run and budget from usage. The out-of-scope restriction prevents widening org-chart to add several likely configuration fields. Without an explicit mapping, implementation may silently substitute zeroes or infer values contrary to the “not measured” requirement.
findings.suggestion: Write a field-by-field source table before coding: each stat’s source, measured condition, display format, and exact “not measured” representation. If no existing route/source supports parallel, projects, or runs, render those figures as explicitly unmeasured and test that this remains true even when usage exists, consistent with the acceptance criterion that usage fills only the budget figure.

findings.finding: Widening `MarkdownEditorModal` from hardcoded project file operations to injected load/save operations can regress all existing project-scoped editing behavior, including conflict handling, reset behavior on changing target documents, and error rendering. The plan says the state machine remains unchanged, but does not include regression coverage for its existing caller.
findings.suggestion: Keep the injected pair narrowly typed and preserve the existing project caller through an adapter/default implementation rather than duplicating modal logic. Add regression tests for the existing project Markdown editor, including successful save, stale ETag/checksum conflict, and reopening a different document after an error or conflict.

findings.finding: The role extraction rule—“first sentence of the first non-heading paragraph”—needs deterministic handling for Markdown constructs such as blockquotes, lists, code fences, abbreviations, links, and paragraphs without conventional sentence punctuation. A simplistic regex can expose markup or truncate unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the project’s Markdown parser if available and extract text nodes from the first eligible paragraph, excluding headings/code blocks. Define a bounded fallback for punctuation-free text and return `measured:false` for empty/non-prose content. Unit-test representative charter examples.

findings.finding: The type-mirror plan correctly adds a drift guard, but `server/src/types/org.ts` is described as canonical while re-exporting definitions from `external/org/`. That is acceptable only if route responses use those same types and the client sync test compares the actual serialized route contracts, not just similarly named TypeScript interfaces.
findings.suggestion: Make `server/src/types/org.ts` the sole server import path for the route and explicitly test the JSON-visible response shapes, including all discriminated error and `measured` variants. Keep the client mirror test focused on field-level API compatibility rather than relying on nominal type names.  Overall, the direct in-process reuse of existing org readers is a good, low-duplication approach, and the explicit treatment of unsupported “waiting on you” is sound. The change needs an access-control decision and strict file-path authorization before implementation, plus clearer partial-failure and stats/document-view contracts. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The fix for a previously-reported finding (AuditLogModal's queryFn side effect duplicating rows on background refetch) added refetchOnMount:false/refetchOnReconnect:false/refetchOnWindowFocus:false, but this also disabled the FOREGROUND refetch TanStack Query would do on a genuine remount with cached data. Since LeadCard.tsx conditionally unmounts AuditLogModal on close ({auditOpen && <AuditLogModal .../>}), reopening the same lead's audit log within the default 5-minute gcTime remounts the component with local `pages` state reset to [] while the cached query never re-invokes queryFn (so the side effect that populated `pages` never fires) -- the modal renders a completely blank body with no loading/error/not-found state. 100% reproducible on every close-then-reopen cycle.
findings.suggestion: Stop deriving entries from a queryFn side effect. Fetch each page via its own query (e.g. useQueries keyed per cursor) and derive entries directly from each query's data, so a cache hit on remount renders immediately with no side effect required. Add a regression test: open, close (unmount), reopen with the same QueryClient, assert entries are still visible.

Run it, per the medium+ convention.

The hook and nav-gating consumers were tested elsewhere, but nothing verified the page's own render logic for each of the 4 presence states.
findings.suggestion: Add OrgPage.test.tsx mocking useOrgChartPresence/useOrgChart/useOrgRoster, asserting each presence branch renders its test id and that DOM order holds (org-chart -> org-shared-docs -> org-lead-list) in the present case.

findings.finding: The PUT charter route's HIGH external-review fix refuses a syntactically-valid-but-unregistered leadId via an org-chart membership check, but the two GET routes for a lead's learnings.md and audit.jsonl only shape-validated leadId (LEAD_ID_RE) and never checked chart membership -- inconsistent posture; a stale/decommissioned lead directory still on disk would still serve through the browser-facing proxy.
findings.suggestion: Add the same chart-membership check to both GET handlers for consistency with the charter PUT route's posture, or explicitly document the narrower scope as intentional (read-only, local-only, host-allowlist-gated).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: requireChartLead's LEAD_ID_RE shape-check, deferring to the downstream core's own re-validation of the same raw leadId string, is a sufficient gate for all three routes it guards (the two GET routes and the PUT charter route). — False for the PUT route. resolveOrgAllowlistedTarget derives its own, more lenient leadId by slicing the path.resolve()-normalized absolute path, while Hono's route-param decode applies tryDecodeURIComponent (which decodes %2f to a literal '/') but getPath()'s path segmentation uses decodeURI (which leaves %2f encoded). A raw leadId of 'ghost-lead/' (from URL segment 'ghost-lead%2f') fails LEAD_ID_RE (trailing slash), but resolveOrgAllowlistedTarget's path-normalized derivation collapses it to the clean, chart-registered 'acme-lead'-shaped target. Deferring on the LEAD_ID_RE rejection let the PUT proceed with NO chart-membership check at all — an unregistered/decommissioned lead's charter.md could be written through the allowlisted path despite requireChartLead existing specifically to prevent that.
findings.suggestion: Reject (400 invalid_lead_id) directly on a raw-string LEAD_ID_RE failure instead of deferring to the downstream core, for all three call sites uniformly. LEAD_ID_RE matches only [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* (no '/' or '.'), so a raw string that passes it can never diverge from its own path-normalized form — rejecting here closes the whole class, not just the %2f PoC. Verified by reverting the fix and confirming the new regression test (org.test.ts, the '%2f-suffixed leadId' case) failed with a 409 instead of the expected 400; restoring the fix made it pass.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: AuditLogModal's per-cursor-page useQueries architecture (the code-review fix for the blank-on-remount regression) is safe against concurrent user interaction with the pagination control. — Two gaps found. (1) A rapid double-click on 'Load older entries' fires both click handlers before either state update is reflected in a re-render, so both computed the same `next` cursor from the same stale `lastQuery` closure and both appended it — a duplicate cursor entry, meaning a wasted duplicate fetch and (had entries differed page-to-page) a duplicated page of results. (2) Reading only `queries[0]`'s error hid a failure on any page after the first: existing rows just sat there with no error UI and no way to retry the specific page that failed, and the prior loadOlder() logic re-derived the next cursor from `lastQuery.data?.nextCursor` which is undefined on a failed page, silently re-fetching page ONE into a new slot instead of retrying the page that actually failed.
findings.suggestion: Idempotent cursor push via the functional state updater (prev[prev.length-1] === next ? prev : [...prev, next]) to de-dupe the double-click race; derive `error` from `queries.find(q => q.error)?.error` instead of queries[0] only; and have loadOlder() call `.refetch()` on the failed last page instead of re-deriving a cursor when `lastFailed` is true. Verified via two new regression tests (AuditLogModal.test.tsx, 'doubt-review fixes' describe block) covering the double-click dedup and the per-page-error-then-Retry flow; both pass, and the full 368-file/3469-test client suite remains green.

findings.finding: The browser write route authorizes only that the synthesized path `${leadId}/charter.md` has kind `charter`; it never verifies that `leadId` exists in the parsed `org-chart.json` or that this is that lead’s declared `charter_path`. Any syntactically valid lead ID with an existing allowlisted charter path can therefore be written through the plain browser surface, including an unregistered/stale lead directory. It also fails valid charts whose `charter_path` is not the synthesized conventional path.
findings.suggestion: Parse/validate the chart before writing, require `leadId` to be a chart entry, and use/compare its declared `charter_path` against the resolved target. Reject unknown leads and any path mismatch with 403.

findings.finding: GET /api/org/leads` does not satisfy the specified “parse the chart once” composite-read behavior. `buildCadence()` calls `readLeadOrgInfo()` for every lead, and `lastRunCore()` called by `buildNow()` parses it again when a last-run file exists. This recreates the synchronous per-lead chart-read pattern the composite endpoint was explicitly intended to remove.
findings.suggestion: Derive cadence/cron and the information needed for last-run staleness from the chart parsed at the start of the request, passing the parsed lead data into the per-lead builders rather than invoking `readLeadOrgInfo()`.

findings.finding: The Resting Now state renders an absolute locale timestamp (`new Date(...).toLocaleString()`), while the specified Now contract requires “Last active {relative time}.” This will display values such as a calendar date/time instead of “Last active 2 hours ago.”
findings.suggestion: Use the project’s relative-time formatter, or add a bounded relative-time formatter, for `lastRunAt`.

findings.finding: Missing shared files do not produce the required visible “not found” state. `orgFileReadCore()` runs `realPathGuard()` before opening the file, so a nonexistent allowlisted target returns `400 path_traversal` rather than `404 not_found`; the viewer consequently renders its generic error state, not `org-doc-viewer-not-found`. The server test explicitly encodes this incompatible behavior.
findings.suggestion: Preserve containment checks while distinguishing absence from traversal—e.g., open safely first and then perform real-path validation for an existing file—or map the known missing-target response to a visible not-found state in the shared-doc viewer.

findings.finding: The required client/server type mirror is incomplete. The canonical server defines `LastRunResponse`, `BeatRegisterHealthResponse`, and `BeatRegisterEntryView`, but `orgApi.ts` does not mirror them and the sync test does not compare them. This directly contradicts the specified mirrored-shapes list and means changes to those route contracts can drift without the intended guard failing.
findings.suggestion: Add verbatim client definitions for all canonical org route shapes, including these unions/interfaces, and extend the schema-sync test to compare their interface fields and union arms.

findings.finding: The purported AC-10 test does not test refusal of non-charter org-file writes. It submits an invalid traversal-like `leadId` and accepts either 400 or 403, so it would still pass if a legitimate `decision_log.md` or `decisions-proposed.md` write path were exposed and writable.
findings.suggestion: Exercise attempted writes to each prohibited allowlisted kind through the new browser proxy using valid fixture data, assert exactly 403, and add a valid-but-unregistered lead-ID case to prevent the authorization gap in the write route.

findings.finding: Required behavior tests are missing. There is no CommandCenter test proving its palette filtering consumes the presence state, and no Org edit-flow test proving Edit opens `MarkdownEditorModal`, loads fresh charter content, and saves with the loaded ETag in `If-Match`. The existing LeadCard test only checks a disabled pause button and static card values, so a broken override/save integration or an always-visible palette Org entry would pass.
findings.suggestion: Add a CommandCenter test for absent/present/broken filtering and an Org-page edit integration test that mocks load/save, asserts the modal test ID and fresh load, then verifies the PUT request’s `If-Match` header. Add the specified present/missing E2E flow as well.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The page structure is largely in place, but the charter-write authorization is too broad and several explicit composite-read, document-state, type-mirror, and required-test contracts are not met. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
